chunks: And it is narrated from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, that he said:

I said: A man performs sajdah while he is wearing a cap or a turban. So he said: “If something from his forehead touches the ground, in the area between his eyebrows and the edge of his hairline, then it has sufficed for him.”

The first part of the Book of Salat is complete, and it is followed in the second part by the chapter on the acts for the night of Jumu‘ah and its day. And praise belongs to Allah as is the due of His praise, and blessings be upon the best of His creation, Muhammad and his pure family, and Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Trustee.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَهُ: it sufficed him, meaning it fulfilled the requirement
key_terms.الْأَرْضَ: the ground, the surface touched in prostration
key_terms.جَبْهَتِهِ: his forehead, the required place of contact in sajdah
key_terms.حَاجِبَيْهِ: his two eyebrows, marking part of the forehead area

ai.seo_question: Is sajdah valid if part of the forehead is covered by a cap or turban?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning sajdah when a person is wearing a cap or turban. It states that if any part of the forehead within the required area touches the ground, the sajdah is valid; the closing line marks the end of a section of the Book of Salat.
